what: Tables 1 and 2 of Ashrafyan–Gomes (arXiv:2403.02785v2, §8) re-decided: the two analytic solutions the paper tests against are enclosed in interval arithmetic (every π, e, sin, cos, tanh, cube root and integral with its rounding), the semi-Lagrangian scheme is written from the paper and run on the paper's four meshes at the paper's tolerance and at a tight one, and every printed relative error is met by an interval and given a verdict
statement: The exact price of test 1, ϖ = −Q + (1 − t)/4 − ∫ₜ¹∫₀ˢQ, satisfies the clearing identity ϖ + a₁ + 2a₂K = −Q at 21 times as an interval fact; the value function's constant a₀(0) is enclosed to 6.9e-8. Of the 24 printed cells, 13 are REPRODUCED within their two printed digits by an independent implementation of the scheme, 5 are within 15 % and 6 differ — the value function and density columns of test 1 at the fine meshes, where the port's errors are up to 2.4 times the printed ones, and the price of test 2 at the finest mesh, where the port does better than printed (×0.85). The price column of test 1 is reproduced at every mesh to its two digits. At the finest mesh of test 1 the paper's tolerance ε = 0.004 changes the price error by 39 % against ε = 1e−8: the printed number there is part tolerance. The density printed for both tests, read literally, has a mass above 3.9e+95 on a sliver of width 0.001 just outside |x| = 1/λ and is not a probability density; the integrable reading (support |x| < 1/λ) is the one enclosed.

printed.source: Y. Ashrafyan, D. A. Gomes, A fully-discrete semi-Lagrangian scheme for a price formation MFG model, arXiv:2403.02785v2 (30 Jan 2025), §8, Tables 1 (p. 24) and 2 (p. 27); read from the PDF on 2026-09-07
printed.definition: relative errors in l∞ norms: ϖ over the time grid, u at t = 0 over the space grid, m at t = T over the space grid; ρ = 2h; all cases converging within 4 (test 1) or 3 (test 2) iterations of steps 1–4

printedPrice.test1: ϖ(t) = η(τ − ∫x m̄)(T − t) − η∫ₜᵀ∫₀ˢQ(r) dr ds − cQ(t)

printed.printedDensity: m̂(x) = exp(−1/(1 − (λx)²)) for |x| < 1, 0 otherwise — as printed the exponent is positive and unbounded on 1/λ < |x| < 1 and the integral diverges; the integrable reading is support |x| < 1/λ
